Merlin, an experimental second renderer that renders absolutely everything (not as exact as Kestrel), plus a new default limiter and duplicate notes rendered as one.

## Before you upgrade

- **Renders at the defaults are not the same files as 1.3.0's.** The default limiter is now `balanced`, which takes the mix in 2.5 dB lower and levels sustained loud passages before the brickwall, and duplicate notes are now rendered as one voice at their summed gain. Dense files sound fuller and a little differently loud. `--limiter brickwall` and `--coalesce off` are the nearest way back to 1.3.0.
- **The brickwall limiter has a 20 ms hold now.** On a steady low note it used to distort (about -31 dB total harmonic distortion at 30 Hz); with the hold it doesn't.

## What's new

- **Merlin (Convolution), in Extras and as `--backend merlin`.** Kestrel steps through a song with a pool of voices. Merlin renders one key at a time for the whole song and mixes them, so it has no voice pool and nothing is stolen or dropped. It is very experimental and very heavy: it keeps what it renders on disk while it works (over a hundred gigabytes for the largest file I tried, which took about 23 minutes), and it doesn't promise that a render will finish. It refuses files of 200 GB or more or with more than 25 billion notes, 31-EDO files, `--min-velocity`, per-track renders and more than one soundfont, and it can't be resumed. Ctrl+C stops it and keeps nothing. The guided renderer asks first.
- **Duplicate notes are rendered as one voice** (`--coalesce on`, the default). Notes with the same channel, key, velocity, tick and release, as layered tracks write them, become one voice at their summed gain. It sounds the same to within rounding, and on a dense file much more of it is heard, because fewer voices are stolen or dropped. `--coalesce off` renders every note on its own.
- **A new default limiter, `balanced`.** Between the brickwall's loudness and omni's drag after a loud burst. `brickwall`, `omni` and `off` are still there.
- **`--tempo-timing exact`.** Plays the tempo map as written, the way OmniConverter does, and gives the same length at every `--rate`. The default stays BASSMIDI's timing. `kestrel info` prints both lengths when a file's differ.
- **MIDI reading is faster,** and on a file with thousands of tracks it uses more cores. Nothing a render writes changes because of it.
- **A graphics driver that crashes while Kestrel lists your GPUs costs only that backend,** not the whole start-up. A render opens only the backend of the card it lands on, the environment check is watched like a render, and the machine report reads Windows' own tools correctly on non-English Windows.

## If a render fails

Send the log from `logs` (the guided renderer shows its path). If you can, make a machine report too (Extras → Machine report) and send it privately, not in a public issue.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.4.0-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.4.0-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.4.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

Each download has a GitHub attestation proving it was built from this repository. With the GitHub CLI, `gh attestation verify <file> --repo thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi` checks it.

The macOS build hasn't been tested yet. If you try it, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
